global_read: global.json (12:27) shows the risk tape stabilizing/easing slightly overnight -- Brent $84.57 (+0.4% 1d) is off its recent high, VIX 16.73 (+6.8% 1d) ticked up but is still well below its 1-month range (-9.3% 1mo), S&P/Dow both mildly red (-0.5%/-0.2%), gold +0.44%, PKR/USD 277.3 (+0.73% 1d, PKR weakening a touch), DXY flat -- a mixed-not-panicked global backdrop, but domestically the picture is worse than the tape: SBP reserves just posted a $1.245bn weekly drop (external debt repayment) and Pakistan's own fuel-price and equity-market signals are pointing the wrong way into the weekend.
drivers: US-Iran conflict is escalating again, not de-escalating: Iran fired on a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz and declared it closed, the US retaliated overnight with strikes on multiple Iranian sites, and Iran responded with strikes into Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait and the UAE; Hormuz crossings are down more than half vs the prior week per Kpler shipping data (https://www.npr.org/2026/07/13/nx-s1-5891746/us-iran-strait-of-hormuz-updates, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Strait_of_Hormuz_crisis)

PSX reversed hard into the weekend after Thursday's rebound: KSE-100 opened Friday down ~560 points (-0.31%) to 177,562.67, giving back part of Thursday's +2,837.78pt (+1.62%) rally, with broad-based selling across autos, cement, banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMCs on the renewed US-Iran escalation headlines (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40430486/negative-sentiment-at-psx-kse-100-down-over-500-points, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618665/psx-up-2838-points-on-renewed-risk-appetite)

SBP reserves fell sharply this week: down $1.245bn to $17.226bn as of 2026-07-10 (from $18.471bn), attributed to external debt repayments; total liquid reserves down to $22.676bn from $23.988bn -- a real domestic anchor weakening even before this run, not just a global-tape story (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/16/sbp-reserves-crash-after-big-debt-payment/)

A fresh, larger fuel-price hike is coming: petrol is expected up ~Rs10/litre and HSD diesel up as much as ~Rs40/litre in the fortnightly review effective 2026-07-18, driven by the Hormuz-linked oil spike, with reports of diesel hoarding/shortages at some pumps; govt is weighing a petroleum-levy cut to soften the blow (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/17/petrol-and-diesel-prices-likely-to-increase-today/, https://profit.pakistantoday.com.pk/2026/07/17/petrol-prices-may-rise-rs10-diesel-rs40-per-litre)

Domestic policy anchors otherwise unchanged and re-verified this cycle: SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% on 2026-06-15 and confirmed the FY27 MPC calendar with the next decision on 2026-07-27 (https://propakistani.pk/2026/06/23/sbp-to-announce-first-monetary-policy-decision-of-fy27-on-july-27/); CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June 2026 from 11.7% in May, next print due 2026-08-01 (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40428026/pakistan-inflation-hits-111-in-june-2026); IMF EFF/RSF program on track, $4.8bn disbursed after the 3rd/2nd reviews (2026-05-08), 4th review expected September 2026 (https://khybernews.tv/imf-to-provide-pakistan-3-6-billion-more-over-next-14-months/)

REGIME CALL: risk-off, downgraded from neutral. Rationale -- (1) the Hormuz conflict has crossed a new threshold overnight: Iran struck a commercial vessel and formally declared the strait closed, the US hit multiple Iranian sites in response, and Iran retaliated into four Gulf states (Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, UAE) -- this is a materially wider and more dangerous escalation than the prior cycle's tanker/Tunb-Island strikes, reversing the fragile 'contained' read; (2) PSX itself confirmed the downgrade by giving back Thursday's rally at the open today (-0.31%, broad sectoral selling) -- the local buy-the-dip divergence that argued for neutral has broken; (3) SBP reserves posted a real $1.245bn weekly drop on debt repayments, a genuine domestic anchor weakening independent of the geo overlay; (4) a large, imminent fuel-price hike (petrol +Rs10, diesel +Rs40) compounds inflation/consumer and OMC-margin risk into next week; (5) desk georisk conflict factor remains maxed at 100 with energy-shock still elevated. Domestic monetary/fiscal anchors (SBP on hold, CPI easing, IMF program on track) remain constructive in isolation but are outweighed this cycle by an actively widening regional conflict plus a confirmed equity reversal and a reserves setback. Per desk rules, risk-off caps new setups at 2 and restricts to defensive sectors only.

favored: E&P (upstream oil & gas -- direct beneficiary of elevated realized crude/gas prices while Brent holds near $84-86 and the Hormuz premium persists)
banks (quality/defensive, high-rate carry, sub-policy-rate T-bill funding costs supportive of margins)
fertilizer (domestic-demand defensive, low direct oil-import beta, though today's open showed sector-wide selling -- treat as relative-defensive, not immune)
avoid: OMCs (inventory/margin and circular-debt risk from a large imminent fuel hike -- petrol +Rs10, diesel +Rs40 -- with hoarding/shortage reports already surfacing)
autos (imported-input cost + weaker consumer demand under fuel/inflation pressure, sold off hard at today's open)
cement (energy-cost sensitive, sold off at today's open)
textiles/exporters (Gulf freight-cost and shipping-route exposure while Hormuz crossings remain down more than half vs the prior week)
